title: Multiple nitrogen reservoirs in a protoplanetary disk at the epoch of comet and giant planet formation
question: Do HCN and CN trace distinct nitrogen isotopic reservoirs in the TW Hya disk, and does HCN/HC15N vary with radius (selective photodissociation)?

data.sensitivity: 2.3, 1.9, 2.0 mJy/beam per 61 kHz channel (HCN, H13CN, HC15N)

what.value: TW Hya disk density/temperature model used to bound density

evidence.quote: Referring to the TW Hya model of (cite: vanthoff2017), this upper limit indicates that the density is at these radii higher than
is significantly higher than the / ratio of $65\pm10$ in the local ISM (cite: halfen2017)
agrees surprisingly well with the value of 89$\pm1$ in the PSN (cite: clayton2004)
CN/C in the TW Hya system yielded a significantly higher ratio, 323$\pm$30 (Paper I)

recipe.method: CASA pipeline, export to Gildas, self-calibration

recipe.goal: Spatially averaged line fluxes in Keplerian masks
recipe.method: Mask where HCN 354507.455 MHz hf line >40 mJy/beam per channel, exclude r<0.3''; average spectra; Gaussian fit weak hf lines; HCN flux = average corrected by 4.2% relative intensity
assumptions: Optically thin lines, equal excitation temperature, flux ratio = column density ratio within 1%

recipe.method: Combine Keplerian and annular masks, 5 au wide annuli from 5 to 55 au in 5 au steps, rms-weighted averaging, Gaussian fits; power law fit to HCN/HC15N
1D ALICO non-LTE calculations with hf overlap, densities and 5-30 K; FWHM-based upper limit on Tkin ~35 K

evidence.quote: The best fit of a power law to the HCN/HC gives 117$\pm$10$\times(r/20\,\au)^{1.3\pm0.13}$

answer_key.quantity: Upper limit kinetic temperature at r>=35 au

evidence.quote: places an upper limit on the kinetic temperature of $(FWHM/2.35)^2\times\mu \mh/(2k_B)\approx$35 K
